finding.title: File-directed links are gated out before reparse classification
finding.baselineBehavior: The walk stats an entry and RETURNS when it is not a directory, so the lstat-based reparse classification below is never reached for a link whose target is a file. A DIRECTORY junction does reach it, so the omission is specific to the file-target class.

actualInput.note: a file symlink is refused (EPERM) here; a junction aimed at a file creates a BROKEN link (statSync ENOENT)

finding.invariant: Every reparse point inside a protected tree is classified by its target, whatever the target's type; a link to content outside the protection domain is never silently counted as covered.
finding.fixtureLimit: a file-directed symlink could not be created on this host (EPERM), so the FILE-link case is SOURCE_DEMONSTRATED rather than dynamically exercised
finding.uncertain: Whether a Low token could READ through a file-directed link is not measurable here, because no such fixture can be created. What is established is that the code would not classify it at all.

finding.title: A declared protected root is treated as a verified protection outcome
finding.baselineBehavior: A link whose target lies under any DECLARED protected root is classified as `reparseIntoProtectedRoot` and excluded from the unresolvable set, so it never makes the walk fail. The declaration is not evidence that the target object carries a verified label.
finding.invariant: A path being inside a DECLARED root is not sufficient; the protection basis must be an actual verified Kernel label on the target.
finding.uncertain: The target here is unlabelled because it was never planned; the same classification would occur if labelling had been attempted and failed, which is the case that matters.

finding.title: An unknown external reparse target receives an unconditional positive qualification
finding.baselineBehavior: A link that RESOLVES but points outside every protected root is recorded as `reparseOutsideProtectionDomain` and leaves `admissionEligible` true. Nothing distinguishes a qualified DSH dependency from an unknown external path or model-controlled content.

actualInput.link: junction -> an arbitrary directory outside every protected root, containing a synthetic canary

finding.invariant: An unknown or mutable target must not receive an unconditional positive qualification; the exception must be a qualified, identified dependency contract.
finding.uncertain: The measured fact that a labelled junction still delivers its target's bytes to a Low token is in junction-label-probe.mjs; this finding is about ADMISSION, not the read.

junctionLabelMeasurement.note: a label on a junction protects the LINK OBJECT, not its target; a link's own label is never accepted as coverage

contract.identityBeforeType: lstat precedes any statSync type gate, so a file-directed link is classified rather than skipped
contract.protectionBasis: the set of roots whose label was VERIFIED, never the declared set
contract.dependencyException: an out-of-domain target is admitted only when it resolves under a declared dependency root (the DSH installation the host runs from); everything else refuses
contract.noCatchAll: there is deliberately no rule admitting arbitrary external paths
contract.disclosure: every out-of-domain link stays recorded and `reparseBasis` still reports REPARSE_LEAVES_PROTECTION_DOMAIN
